title: Transposition and musical creation
description: Move music by semitones, numerals, or degrees — then write a short piece on purpose.

cards.back: Moving music to a different pitch level while keeping internal relationships: the same intervals, scale degrees, and Roman numerals.

cards.front: What does creation mean in this lesson?
cards.back: Using what you know deliberately: key, form, harmony, voice leading, melody, and feel — then revising.

cards.front: Transpose C Am F G7 up three semitones.
cards.back: Eb Cm Ab Bb7. Move every pitch class up n semitones along C C# D Eb E F F# G Ab A Bb B.

cards.front: Why is transposing by Roman numerals usually better than shifting each chord?
cards.back: Write I vi IV V once, then respell in the new key. Faster and less error-prone, and it works for any key you can spell.

cards.front: Spell I vi IV V in C, G, D, A, and E.
cards.back: C Am F G. G Em C D. D Bm G A. A F#m D E. E C#m A B.

cards.front: E G A G in C major is degrees 3 5 6 5. What is it in G and in F?
cards.back: In G: B D E D. In F: A C D C. Keep scale degrees, not fret numbers.

cards.front: When can you slide a melody to transpose, and when must you recheck notes?
cards.back: If it lies on one string set with no open strings, slide by the same number of frets. On a different string set the G–B gap changes the shape, so check the notes.

cards.front: What does a capo at fret n do? What does G with capo 2 sound as?
cards.back: It raises every open string by n semitones. A G shape at fret 2 sounds as A major.

cards.front: Why can’t open shapes slide along the neck the way barre shapes can?
cards.back: Open strings stay the same pitch. Barre shapes and shells can move.
1. Key and mood. 2. Form (8 or 12 bars). 3. Harmony with a function plan and one color. 4. Voice leading. 5. Feel and pulse. 6. Melody / motif. 7. Outline the changes. 8. Revise the weakest bar.

cards.front: In the sample G-major 8-bar plan, what are E7 and Cm7 doing?
cards.back: E7 is V7/ii, a secondary dominant aimed at Am7. Cm7 is iv7, borrowed from G minor, darkening the IV.

cards.front: Slide C-major ii V I shells (x5x56x, 3xx46x, x3x45x) up two frets.
cards.back: D major: Em7 x7x78x, A7 5xx68x, Dmaj7 x5x67x. Shape stays; roots move.

cards.front: Play G Em C D with capo 2. What key and chords sound?
cards.back: A major: A F#m D E.

cards.front: Transpose Dm7 G7 Cmaj7 to F, G, and Eb.
cards.back: Gm7 C7 Fmaj7. Am7 D7 Gmaj7. Fm7 Bb7 Ebmaj7.

cards.front: Transpose E A B A (a blues fragment) from E to A.
C Am F G7 as numerals, then in A and in Eb.
cards.back: I vi IV V7. In A: A F#m D E7. In Eb: Eb Cm Ab Bb7.
